scope: Tenth expansion batch: 12 exercises, three each for conformity with toori/doori, guidance or governing conditions with moto, additive ue ni, and a completed preliminary step with ue de. The moto target has two person-guidance/supervision items and one conditions item; it does not claim three examples of each sub-use. Hoka is not included.

sources.section: Conformity/sameness use of toori; direct attachment after plain and past verbs; noun + no toori and voiced noun + doori. The interchangeable noun patterns support accepting both 予定どおり and 予定のとおり, not adding no or voicing after every preceding form.

Inspected JSON entry slug 下-1, reading もと, spellings 下 and 許: first sense under guidance/supervision/rules/law, with no moto ni/de; third sense under a promise/condition/assumption, commonly no moto ni. Spelling recognition is not a claim that both spellings are equally frequent. Do not use the separate 元-2 former/ex entry as evidence for this sense.

Additive ue ni; verb/i-adjective direct attachment, na-adjective + na, and noun + no; possible omission of ni. The exercises use compatible favorable features, but do not adopt the source's unqualified always-same-evaluation restriction.

Completed preliminary step before a subsequent action; past verb or noun + no attachment, often formal and implying a logical requirement. The source's categorical exclusion of passive clauses is not adopted.

authoringNotes: All examples are newly authored. References establish construction patterns and spellings; sentence naturalness, exact blank spans and answer feedback require independent linguistic review.

Six questions visibly restrict the noun list to toori or moto, allowing necessary no and voicing. They cover noun + no toori, a direct noun compound with doori (also accepting no toori), a past verb + toori, and noun + no moto de. The printed ni/de is part of each supplied frame, not an independently tested particle.

Six questions instead request only ni or de after printed ue. The past-verb additive example deliberately prevents a false rule that a preceding past form always determines ue de. The future-decision example prevents interpreting subordinate ta-form as necessarily completed at the present time.

Screen the full article inventory. You and mama can overlap with conformity; ato/sue can describe related temporal sequences; hoka can add information. Such alternatives are excluded by explicit question-side form restrictions, not by a claim that they are universally ungrammatical.

Omission of ni in additive ue is grammatical, but an empty answer is not part of the task requesting one of the two written particles. This set does not teach every use of ue de, including the distinct in-doing/in-the-course-of use.

All prior 131 exercise records remain unchanged. One SRS identity per exercise, not per spelling, missing-particle form or choose/type presentation. These controlled contrasts are not unrestricted discrimination across the entire noun inventory.
